role.altitude: The climate policy analyst keeps choosing what to push, reading and comparing policies, building arguments, meeting officials and designing programmes; rebuilding contact lists, screening long search results one by one, formatting references and typing up feedback forms shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting stop rules for assisted screening
Opening every cited source before use
role.ambitious_version: An analyst who reads more policies more closely because the search and screening take a fraction of the time.

tasks.short: Choose the initiative and audience, keep the stakeholder list, write the position paper, draft, approve and send outreach letters, meet government or environmental groups to promote initiatives to mitigate climate change, and record follow-ups.

steps.what: Analyst decides which initiative to promote and to whom
Analyst builds the list of officials and groups to contact
Analyst writes the position paper on the initiative
Analyst writes outreach letters to government and environmental groups
Analyst checks the final letters and recipient list: each letter's text and tailored paragraph against the position paper, and each recipient
Analyst sends the letters
Analyst meets officials and groups to promote the initiative
Analyst records contacts and follow-ups: in a spreadsheet today; in the register after the change, where sent letters are logged by the merge and meeting notes are still written by the analyst

tasks.design: A shared contact register holds officials and groups with their topics and past contacts, so the list for each initiative is a filter instead of a spreadsheet rebuilt from mailboxes. Letters are merged from a template with each recipient's name and topic, and the analyst adds a tailored paragraph. The analyst approves the final letters and recipient list, then sends that version. Choosing the initiative, the position paper and the meetings stay with the analyst. Sent letters are logged in the register by the merge; the analyst still writes meeting notes and follow-ups there.

approvals.approved_version: The letters with their text and the recipient list exactly as checked by the analyst in s5, sent once by e-mail to the recipients on that list; any change to text or recipients needs a new check before sending.

tasks.previous_blocker: Contacts sat in personal mailboxes and spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared contact registers with mail merge.
tasks.still_hard: Officials reached only through personal networks.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which official will champion the initiative.

reach.learn: Whether outreach reaches the right people.

evidence.claim: Shared contact registers with mail merge replace spreadsheet contact lists.

assumptions: Boundary: promoting initiatives; written materials to inform government (task 16850) and presenting at meetings (task 16843) are sibling tasks.
s3 is part of preparing written materials for government and groups, which sibling task 16850 covers; its saving is counted there.
The contact register holds business contact data with a lawful basis; personal notes are kept to what outreach needs.
Deciding, approving, sending and meeting keep their full time. s8 keeps 80 because meeting notes and follow-ups are a first record; only logging sent letters goes.
unknowns: Number of outreach rounds per year.
research_questions: Do more contacts lead to meetings?

incremental.description: Analyst keeps the contact register current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the register is incomplete, so lists are partly rebuilt (s2 keeps 80), and most letters are tailored (s4 keeps 90) (4.2); high: register and template as designed (9.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define the question, search for policies, practices or procedures for climate or environmental management, screen the results, read and compare the relevant ones, and record findings with sources.

steps.what: Analyst defines the research question and search terms
Analyst searches policy databases and literature for policies, practices or procedures

loop.input: The search plan and indexed policy documents and abstracts.
loop.output: A ranked list with short summaries, each linked to its source.
loop.check: The analyst opens every cited source before use; summaries are never quoted.
loop.stop: The analyst runs the manual search when the list misses a known key source.
loop.why_not_simpler: Policy documents use varied terms across countries.

steps.what: Analyst screens the results for relevance

loop.input: Titles and abstracts of the search results.
loop.output: The results reordered so the likely relevant come first, while the analyst labels each one read.
loop.check: The stop rule, fixed beforehand, is tested on known relevant records before use.
loop.stop: Screening stops when the fixed rule is met; below it the analyst screens on.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevance depends on the question and changes per study.

steps.what: Analyst reads and compares the relevant policies and practices
Analyst records findings in a comparison table with sources

loop.input: The relevant documents and the table's fields.
loop.output: Proposed field values with the quoted passage and page for each.
loop.check: The analyst checks each value against its quoted passage.
loop.stop: Fields without a matching passage stay empty for the analyst to fill.
loop.why_not_simpler: Documents present the same facts in different places.

tasks.design: A search tool returns ranked documents with short linked summaries, and the analyst opens every source before using it. An active learning screener reorders results while the analyst labels them, with a stop rule fixed and tested beforehand. Reading and comparing stay with the analyst. An extraction step proposes table fields with the quoted passage and page, and the analyst checks each one.
tasks.previous_blocker: Long result lists were screened one by one and tables typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Assisted screening and search summaries with citations.
tasks.still_hard: Policies published only in national languages or as scanned PDFs.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that two similar policies work very differently in practice.

ambition.what: Update comparisons when policies change instead of once per study.

tasks.altitude: Less sifting; reading and comparing stay.

evidence.claim: On one published review of 5,808 references, active learning found all 28 included studies after screening 746, in 92 minutes against 1,018.
An open-source screener reorders abstracts while a person screens.
A literature database gives summaries citing up to 20 papers and warns against relying on them alone.
In 84 generated literature reviews, 18% to 55% of references were fabricated.

assumptions: Boundary: researching policies and practices; gathering climate studies from agencies and labs (task 16846) and reviewing legislation for impacts (task 16848) are sibling tasks.
Policy searches return hundreds, not thousands, of documents, so s3 is priced well below the published benchmark.
Defining the question and reading keep their full time.
research_questions: Does assisted screening miss any source a full manual screen finds?

already_counted.description: Analyst opens and checks every cited source.

incremental.description: Analyst tests the stop rule on known relevant records.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: narrow questions where screening is done by hand (s3 keeps 100) and summaries help little (s2 keeps 80) (9.0); high: broad searches with the screener as designed (24.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Outline the argument, write the sections, make figures and tables, format references, revise after comments, approve and submit reports or academic papers on findings of climate-related studies.

steps.what: Analyst outlines the paper and its argument
Analyst writes the sections of the report or academic paper

loop.input: The outline, the analyst's notes and the results tables.
loop.output: Draft text for methods and results sections.
loop.check: Every number must match a results table and references come only from the analyst's reference library; the analyst reads each drafted claim against the result and source it rests on.
loop.stop: The analyst writes the section by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: The argument and wording are specific to each study.

steps.what: Analyst makes figures and tables from the results
Analyst formats references and the manuscript to the journal's style
Analyst revises the paper after co-author and reviewer comments
Analyst checks the final manuscript: text, figures and references against the results, and the journal it goes to
Analyst submits the manuscript to the journal or publisher

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript text, figures and reference list exactly as checked by the analyst in s6, submitted once to the submission system of the journal named in it; any change needs a new check before submitting.

tasks.design: The analyst outlines the argument. A drafting step writes first versions of methods and results sections from the analyst's notes and result tables; every number must match a table and references come only from the analyst's reference library, never generated. Figures and tables come from a script that reruns when results change. The reference manager and journal template format the manuscript. Revising, approving and submitting stay with the analyst.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were rebuilt by hand and references formatted manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Scripted figures, reference managers and drafting checked against results.
tasks.still_hard: Discussion sections where the argument is the contribution.
tasks.human_edge: Framing findings so policymakers act on them.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting and redrawing; argument stays.

evidence.claim: In 84 generated literature reviews, 18% to 55% of references were fabricated, so references come only from the analyst's library.
Scripted pipelines and report templates prepare charts and graphs deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary: reports and academic papers on studies; memoranda and briefs for government (task 16850) are a sibling task.
Outlining, revising, approving and submitting keep their full time.
research_questions: Are papers submitted sooner without more reviewer corrections?

incremental.description: Analyst keeps the figure script current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: argument-heavy papers where drafted sections are mostly rewritten (s2 keeps 95) (14.5); high: data-heavy reports drafted as designed (20.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree goals with partners, design educational or outreach programs on climate change, write materials, plan sessions with online registration, and evaluate from feedback.

steps.what: Analyst agrees goals and audience with partners
Analyst designs the educational content and activities
Analyst writes the materials: session texts, handouts and web pages

loop.input: The programme design and an approved fact sheet.
loop.output: Draft texts at the audience's reading level.
loop.check: Every figure and claim must come from the fact sheet; the analyst reads each text against the fact sheet entry it uses and its limits, and edits under their own name.
loop.stop: The analyst writes the text by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each audience needs its own wording.

steps.what: Analyst plans sessions, venues and registrations
Analyst checks the registration form before it opens: session dates, venues, places and the confirmation text
Analyst opens the checked registration form on the programme page
Participant registers on the online form
Participant fills in the online feedback form after the session
Analyst evaluates the programme from participant feedback

tasks.design: Agreeing goals and designing the programme stay with the analyst. A drafting step writes texts at the audience's reading level from an approved fact sheet, and the analyst edits them under their own name. The analyst checks the registration form and opens it once; participants register on it, and it confirms their place and fills the session lists, instead of the analyst handling mails. Participants give feedback on an online form that summarises results, instead of paper forms typed into a spreadsheet.

approvals.approved_version: The registration form with session dates, venues, places and confirmation text exactly as checked by the analyst in s4b, published once on the programme page; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Registrations came by mail and feedback forms were typed in.
tasks.enabler_now: Online registration and feedback forms and drafting from a fact sheet.
tasks.still_hard: Audiences reached only through local partners.
tasks.human_edge: Making climate change concrete for a sceptical group.

reach.learn: Whether more people register and return feedback.

evidence.claim: AI text informing the public must be disclosed unless reviewed under a person's editorial responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: developing programmes; presenting at meetings (task 16843) and grant applications (task 16845) are sibling tasks.
Participants' form time is shown in s5 (registering) and s5b (feedback), each at share 1. s3 keeps 75 because the analyst still rewrites texts for the audience and checks meaning.
s6 saves typing paper feedback forms into a spreadsheet; reading the feedback stays.
Agreeing goals and designing keep their full time.
research_questions: Does feedback response rise with online forms?

incremental.description: Analyst keeps the fact sheet current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many participants keep registering by mail (s4 keeps 80) and drafts need heavy rework (s3 keeps 90) (10.7); high: online registration and drafting as designed (18.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
